stem: A 9-year-old boy cannot sit still in class, blurts out answers, interrupts others and loses his homework. His parents see the same at home, and it has been going on for 2 years. Hearing, vision and the physical examination are normal.
oneliner: 9M + 2 y fidgety, blurts out, interrupts, disorganized + at school and home + normal exam → first-line drug works how?
ask: The first-line drug for this condition works mainly by which of the following?

options.B: Increasing release of dopamine and norepinephrine

whyNot.A: **Propranolol**: tremor, performance anxiety; does not treat inattention
whyNot.C: **Benzodiazepines**: sedate and can worsen behavior in children
whyNot.D: **SSRIs**: depression and anxiety, not first line here

answer: Increased release of dopamine and norepinephrine (stimulants)
why: **Inattention + hyperactivity + impulsivity in two settings for over 6 months** = ADHD. First-line stimulants (**methylphenidate, amphetamine**) **raise synaptic dopamine and norepinephrine**.

drug.name: Methylphenidate / amphetamine
drug.how: Increase synaptic dopamine and norepinephrine (block reuptake; amphetamine also releases them)
drug.watch: Poor appetite and weight loss, insomnia, tachycardia, slowed growth

chain: Block DA and NE reuptake (amphetamine also releases)
More dopamine and norepinephrine in prefrontal synapses

stem: A 39-year-old woman has depression with increased sleep and appetite, marked sensitivity to rejection and prominent phobic anxiety. Two SSRIs failed. She is started on phenelzine.
oneliner: 39F + depression with phobic anxiety, increased sleep and appetite + SSRIs failed + phenelzine started → which brain levels rise?
ask: Which of the following is increased in her presynaptic nerve terminals by this drug?

whyNot.B: Made by glutamate decarboxylase and broken down by **GABA transaminase**, not MAO
whyNot.C: An amino acid **precursor**, not a MAO substrate
whyNot.D: An amino acid **precursor** of catecholamines, not a MAO substrate
whyNot.E: Intermediate made by tyrosine hydroxylase; **dopamine**, not DOPA, is the MAO substrate

why: **Phenelzine** is a **MAO inhibitor**. **MAO breaks down norepinephrine, serotonin and dopamine**, so blocking it raises their stores in the nerve terminal.

drug.name: Phenelzine
drug.how: Irreversibly blocks MAO-A and MAO-B, so monoamines accumulate in nerve terminals
drug.use: Atypical depression, panic, social phobia, treatment-resistant depression
drug.watch: Hypertensive crisis with tyramine, serotonin syndrome, orthostasis, weight gain, 2-week washout

stem: A 27-year-old woman has had recurrent episodes of sudden palpitations, sweating, chest tightness and a fear of dying that peak within 10 minutes. She now avoids shopping malls and public transport. Her physical examination, ECG and thyroid tests are normal. Alprazolam is prescribed for short-term relief while a long-term drug takes effect.
oneliner: 27F + sudden attacks of palpitations, sweating, fear of dying + avoids malls and buses + normal ECG and TSH + alprazolam started → works how?
ask: The drug relieves her attacks mainly by which of the following mechanisms?

options.A: Increasing the frequency of GABA-A chloride channel opening
options.B: Increasing the duration of GABA-A channel opening

whyNot.C: **Buspirone**: slow onset, for generalized anxiety, not panic attacks

answer: Increased frequency of GABA-A chloride channel opening (benzodiazepine)
why: **Abrupt attacks with fear of dying and agoraphobic avoidance** = panic disorder. **Alprazolam**, a benzodiazepine, binds the **GABA-A benzodiazepine site** and **raises the frequency of chloride channel opening**.

drug.name: Alprazolam
drug.how: Positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A; raises frequency of chloride channel opening
drug.watch: Dependence, withdrawal seizures, sedation, respiratory depression with alcohol or opioids; reversed by flumazenil

stem: An 8-year-old boy with spastic cerebral palsy has painful nighttime muscle spasms in his legs. He is given diazepam at bedtime. His mother asks how the drug makes the nerve cells quieter.
oneliner: 8M + spastic cerebral palsy + painful night spasms + diazepam at bedtime → how does it raise GABA effect?
ask: Which of the following best describes how the drug enhances GABA signaling?

options.A: Binding the GABA site itself and opening the channel directly
options.E: Binding a separate site on the GABA-A receptor and increasing GABA-driven chloride channel opening

whyNot.A: That is how a **direct agonist** such as muscimol acts
whyNot.B: **Picrotoxin** does this; it blocks inhibition and causes seizures
whyNot.C: **Vigabatrin**: raises GABA levels in the synapse
whyNot.D: **Tiagabine**: raises synaptic GABA; the drug here acts on the receptor

why: **Diazepam** is a **benzodiazepine** that binds a **separate allosteric site** on the **GABA-A receptor** and makes **GABA open the chloride channel more often**. It needs GABA present.

drug.name: Diazepam
drug.how: Positive allosteric modulator of GABA-A; raises frequency of chloride channel opening only when GABA is bound
drug.use: Anxiety, status epilepticus, muscle spasm, alcohol withdrawal, sedation
drug.watch: Sedation, ataxia, dependence, respiratory depression with alcohol or opioids; reversed by flumazenil
